messages.subject: Inconsistent Warning Message
parts:
I'm running a model in lavaan and I thought I had my final model. When I initially constructed what i thought would be my final model it ran without a problem. Then I was fiddling around with other analyses and I don't remember what happened, but I had to force close R. 

Anyway, today I came back and I needed to extract more information from my final model, but because I had to force close, the fitted model was not saved. Obviously, I still had the syntax so I just ran it again, but this time after fitting the model I was greeted with this lovely message:

Warning message:
In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats, :
lavaan WARNING:
The variance-covariance matrix of the estimated parameters (vcov) does not appear to be positive definite! The smallest eigenvalue (= 2.530586e-17) is close to zero. This may be a symptom that the model is not identified.

I ran the summary anyway and all the numbers appear to be exactly the same as what I was given the other day. The only difference is that I got a warning message today. I know for sure that I did not have a warning the other day because I saved the exact output that I got after running the model initially and there was no warning between the model fit and model summary. I also tried copying the syntax from my saved output and running it, but this too produced a warning. 

What could possibly be the issue? Why did the model run without warning the other day if there was an issue?

I know lavaan gives a warning that it is in beta, so I'm wondering if maybe there is something going on behind the scenes that's inconsistent?

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Inconsistent Warning Message
parts: I ran the summary anyway and all the numbers appear to be exactly the same as what I was given the other day.

Then it is probably not a problem.  If you updated your version of lavaan, then it is probably a newer or more sensitive check than in the version you used to have installed.
